name: textkit
algorithm: Run two of the textkit dogfood's Unicode text tools over a generated text file: grep, counting the lines a case-folded regular expression matches (its bench case's flags, with a pattern this input matches), and wc, counting lines, words, characters, bytes and grapheme clusters by UAX 29 and the widest line in terminal columns (README.md).
notes: Tier A (M9 item 11.32): an Mk-only row, the textkit dogfood unchanged (its bin textkit), compared across mk binaries; no twin (the other languages' std has no UAX 29 or normalization), no defect line (README.md).

The input is tools/bench gen kind words (seed 8, 128,000,000 bytes): ASCII words, spaces and line ends, so the Unicode tables are read but no multi-byte path runs. The quick and publish arguments are one, since a row has one data spec.
The size (data.bytes) is provisional; tools/bench verify -publish-size fixes it in the quiet window, and the checksums change with it.
